text.p: - Slovenia's government decided against lifting electricity and petrol prices. Electrical power companies had been asking for a 13 percent rise.

- Mirjana Markovic, wife of Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic, visited Slovenia on Thursday to promote her new book "Response". This was the first visit of any Serbian politician to Slovenia since it gained independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.

- Ruling centre-left Liberal Democrats said on Thursday that putting together the next government will be a "war of nerves". They want Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek to maintain his post as his party gained the most support in last week's elections.
- Reconstruction of about 1,100 km (671 miles) of damaged roads is expected to cost Slovenia 25 billion tolars ($182.5 million), authorities said.
- Silver Olympic medalist Brigita Bukovec, a runner, and long jumper Gregor Cankar were chosen as best athletes of 1996.
